transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. I'm here because... well, I've barely been sleeping since a warehouse inspection I was on recently. I just lie there replaying bits of it in my head. And when I do finally drift off, I wake up sweaty and wide awake, feeling like I'm right back near that blast.
Can you remember the details of the warehouse inspection incident clearly, or are there parts of it that you just can’t recall?

Well, there are definitely parts I can't recall. I can remember hearing the explosion... and I remember standing outside afterward, looking at the soot on my jacket. But the part in between is just blank. No matter how hard I try to piece it together, I just don't have any memory of how I got outside.
Since the incident, have you found yourself having sudden, vivid memories or flashbacks of the explosion, as if you're reliving it?

Yes, I have. It happens during the day, actually. I'll just be at work, reviewing a policy or looking over a loss report, and out of nowhere I get hit with this really sharp image. I just see the worker on the floor, and all that soot hanging in the air. It's so sudden... it feels like my body just reacts to it before I can even try to stop it.
Since the explosion, have you found yourself avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, I have. Mostly at work... I've been completely avoiding the file for that specific warehouse. And honestly, I've been letting any calls about our other industrial accounts just go straight to voicemail. It's just... even the thought of opening those emails makes my stomach drop, so I just stay away from them as much as I can.
Since the incident, have you noticed yourself feeling ongoing fear, guilt, or anger connected to what happened during the explosion?

Not really, no. I mean, I don't feel guilty or angry about it. It was an accident, you know? I guess I feel a little on edge sometimes, but I wouldn't say I'm walking around feeling scared all day. It's just more about avoiding those specific reminders.
Since the explosion, have you noticed any ongoing feelings of fear, guilt, or anger tied to what happened, even if just in moments?

Like I just said, I don't really feel guilty or angry. I mean, it was a terrible accident, but I don't blame myself or anyone else. And I'm not really walking around feeling terrified all the time either. It's really just when I'm reminded of it, like with those files, that I get that awful feeling. But otherwise, no, I don't have those ongoing feelings you're asking about.

Since the incident, have you noticed yourself feeling emotionally numb, detached from others, or unable to feel positive emotions like joy or happiness, even when you're not thinking about the explosion?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still feel things normally. I mean, I still enjoy spending time with my boyfriend and watching our shows in the evenings. I don't feel numb or disconnected from people at all. Like I said, it's really just the work stuff related to the warehouse that bothers me. Everything else is pretty much normal.
Since the incident, have you had any ongoing sense of fear, anger, or guilt, even in small moments when you're not directly reminded of it?

Doctor, I feel like you've asked me this a few times now. No, I don't have those feelings. Like I said, I'm not angry, and I don't feel guilty. It was an accident. I just get anxious when I have to deal with things that remind me of it, but no, I'm not carrying around fear or anger all day.
Can you think of a time in the past week when you weren’t reminded of the warehouse explosion at all, and if so, did you still feel any lingering fear, anger, or guilt during that time?

I know you're trying to be thorough, but we've really covered this. Yes, there are plenty of times I'm not thinking about the explosion, like over the weekend when I was just hanging out at home. And no, during those times, I don't feel any lingering fear, anger, or guilt. I'm just living my life normally until something specific triggers it.

Since the warehouse explosion, have you noticed any changes in your thoughts or mood, such as increased negative beliefs about yourself, others, or the world, or persistent negative emotional states like sadness or hopelessness?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, I don't feel sad or hopeless at all. And I haven't started thinking negatively about myself or the world, either. Like I've been trying to explain, it's really just the anxiety when I have to deal with things related to the explosion. Aside from that, my mood and the way I think about things haven't changed.
Since the incident, have you ever felt like the world around you felt unreal or detached, as if you were watching things happen from a distance?

No, I haven't felt anything like that. I don't feel detached or like things aren't real. Everything feels perfectly real, it's just... stressful when I'm reminded of what happened. But no, I haven't had any of those spaced-out feelings you're describing.
Since the explosion, have you noticed any changes in your reactivity, like being more irritable, on edge, or having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, I have been a little more irritable, actually. Um, like the other day at work, I snapped at a junior analyst over a really small spreadsheet question. I was way harsher than I meant to be. Afterward, I just felt embarrassed about it, because that’s really not how I usually treat people at all.
Since the explosion, have you found yourself being easily startled or feeling constantly on guard, even in situations where there's no real danger?

Yeah, I definitely have. It's actually been pretty embarrassing at work. Every time a printer jams, or a door slams, or even if someone just walks up behind my desk to ask a question, I jump like something terrible is happening. And it's not just a quick flinch—it takes me several minutes for my heart to stop racing and to actually settle down again.
